text:
jorge.engineer: Hey - returned a rental car yesterday and the company card got charged a $75 "full tank" refuel fee by the agency even though I topped it up before drop-off. I have the self-serve station receipt for $18. Rental agent said the car was recorded as empty on their end. How do we handle the agency charge vs my fill-up receipt?

ana.peopleops: Sorry you hit that, Jorge. We reimburse actual documented fuel purchases. If you have a receipt showing you filled the tank, submit that + the rental agreement showing drop-off odometer and fuel status. Finance will contest the agency charge.

jorge.engineer: I uploaded the fuel receipt but the rental folio just has a generic line "refuel charge $75" and no odometer. The agent said they logged damage/empty tank on their app but wouldn't give me a signed copy.

receipts-bot: receipt uploaded: 2205550040_shell-5th-ave-2025-11-20.jpg

nate.finance: Two steps: 1) Attach your fuel receipt + the rental agreement/return receipt. 2) Add a short attestation: time/place you refueled, pump receipt shows pump ID, and you returned car with fuel in tank. We'll open a dispute with the rental agency.

nate.finance: Policy excerpt: "For rental car fuel disputes, employees must provide a valid merchant receipt for fuel purchase and the rental return confirmation. If the vendor charges a refuel fee, finance will seek reversal from vendor; if reversal fails, reimbursement to employee requires manager approval and documentation."

ana.peopleops: If the rental agency refuses to provide signed return docs, ask them for the "return condition report" or reference number. You can also file a vendor dispute and cc: finance. I can follow up with the rental company contacts we have.

jorge.engineer: I called their corporate line; they gave me a reference #R-998712 but said only the branch manager can release the return report. I've attached a photo of the car fuel gauge at drop-off and a timestamped selfie by the car (shows license plate). Is that ok?

nate.finance: Helpful. Include everything you have. Please put the $75 agency charge as an "out-of-pocket disputed vendor charge" in the expense tool and set status to "dispute - attached docs". Finance will pay you the $18 fuel receipt immediately once manager signs off, and will pursue the $75 with the vendor. If vendor reversal succeeds, we'll adjust the expense. If the vendor won't reverse, we need manager approval for the additional reimbursement.

ana.peopleops: Jorge - ping your manager for quick approval. Also note: in future, when returning at counterless kiosks, take the return confirmation email/screenshots and keep the agent badge/name. It saves time.

jorge.engineer: Thanks. I added the expense entry, marked "dispute", attached pump receipt, photo of gauge + selfie, and the rental reference. Pinged my manager now.

rentals-bot: rental folio uploaded: 2205550100_avis-nyc-return-summary.pdf

nate.finance: Received. We'll start vendor dispute. FYI: if the agency provides a partial credit but not full reversal, finance will apportion per policy and notify you. We'll update the expense thread once we hear back (usually 7-14 business days).

jorge.engineer: Appreciate it. One last Q: are toll transponder charges (EZPass passed to company) handled separately? I had a $3 toll on the same trip and it hit the rental company's merchant.

nate.finance: Tolls billed by rental agency are reimbursable if they are valid trip tolls. Treat them like vendor charges: attach map/snapshot of route + toll notice if possible. Finance will include tolls in the dispute/reimbursement flow.

ana.peopleops: TL;DR: submit receipts + return proof, mark expense as "dispute", manager approval triggers interim reimbursement for documented fuel purchase; finance handles vendor dispute for the excess. Thanks for documenting this thoroughly. :thumbsup:
